— Driving, right of way and sharing rules","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Driving, right of way and sharing rules

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A07
Pass a cyclist as a slow vehicle by crossing the centerline with no oncoming traffic to leave a recommended five feet, or by slowing to the cyclist pace until passing is safe. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A07
Expect cyclists off the shoulder and often in single-file groups that need extra passing time. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A07
Cyclists ride as far right as practical, often eighteen to twenty-four inches into the lane to deter unsafe in-lane passes. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A07
Shared-lane arrow markings guide cyclist position and warn motorists to leave room, differing from bike-lane bicycle symbols. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A07
Motorists grant cyclists full vehicle rights, never deliberately block them, pass only without endangering anyone, and yield inside designated bike lanes. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A07
Cyclists ride single file except on exclusive paths, when passing another bike, two abreast on shoulders or parking lanes, or two abreast on multi-lane roads without extra impedance. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A07
Slower-than-traffic cyclists keep near the right edge except when passing, preparing a left turn, dodging hazards or narrow lanes, or avoiding parked-car doors. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A07
Bicycles often lack mirrors, so drivers treat an approached cyclist as unaware and proceed with extra care. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A05
School bus stopping duties at railroad crossings are set by the cited state statute. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A02
Passing left of the centerline is the two-lane norm, while passing on the right is limited to left-turning vehicles and wide multi-lane pavement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A03
Right-of-way is yielded under the rules, never seized, and every driver must still act to avoid a crash. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-R12 | anchor: A04
An uncontrolled intersection yields to the vehicle on the right, while a four-way stop releases the first arrival after a full stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-R13 | anchor: A04
A stopped driver turns right only with the pedestrian in the opposite half and safe, while following drivers must never pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-R14 | anchor: A06
The funeral lead vehicle obeys intersection controls, while followers behind it may proceed through with reasonable care. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R15 | anchor: A06
Outsider drivers must not split or join a procession for advantage, while procession drivers follow closely without the usual spacing. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec07-R16 | anchor: A01
Town turns need a one-hundred-foot signal and rural turns a three-hundred-foot signal, with the shoulder never a driving lane. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0047]
